judges.routes_note: Routes are alternate vendors for ONE model, tried in order. They are deliberately not separate judges: the same model behind two vendors would satisfy min_judge_models on paper while being one opinion counted twice. The Bailian route runs first because it is the only unblocked one; vendor mixing inside one measurement never happens because a route is picked once up front.

sampling.temperature_note: Deliberately not 0. The manifest aggregates three samples by median, which requires variance to exist. At temperature 0 self_consistency is trivially 1.0 and measures nothing.
sampling.note_local_codex: The local Codex route does not accept a temperature; it uses the CLI provider default and records sampling_control instead. Its self_consistency is therefore measured under different sampling than the HTTP judges and is not directly comparable to theirs.

independence_caveat: Two of the three judges (qwen, zhipu) are Chinese-native families with likely overlapping Chinese training corpora and similar RLHF preferences for Chinese prose; agreement between those two may reflect shared priors rather than independent confirmation. The openai family breaks that correlation and is the reason inter_model_agreement is now interpretable at all — but with one independent rater against two correlated ones, a high alpha still says less than the number suggests. A human rater remains the only fully independent check.
